route_2_sign.text: ROUTE 2: UNDER CONSTRUCTION (mostly done). North: Wi-Fi Dead Zone, then Port City. South: Patch Town.

route_2_north_sign.text: WI-FI DEAD ZONE AHEAD. Port City is on the far side. Signal not guaranteed.

route_2_worker.speaker: Lineworker
route_2_worker.text: We're laying fiber all the way to Port City. Don't trip on the cables.

route_2_worker.speaker: Lineworker
route_2_worker.text: Weird week. Half my crew got an email from someone called R. Now nobody can open their timesheets.

port_arrival.text: Salt air, gull cries, and the hum of a thousand routers. Port City.
The harbor lights flicker. Out on the water, the beacon over Port 443 burns a steady orange.

port_arrival.speaker: Dockworker
port_arrival.text: New hire? Keep your head down. Gray hoodies have been sniffing around the docks all morning.

kevin_docks.speaker: Kevin
kevin_docks.text: {player}! You got that 'mailbox full' email, right? I replied-all with a GIF that explains phishing. It's a fish. Spinning.

kevin_docks.speaker: Kevin
kevin_docks.text: Then everyone replied-all to MY reply. Four hundred people. They clearly needed my expertise.

kevin_docks.speaker: Kevin
kevin_docks.text: Anyway. I'm here for the Networking Cert. I know networking. I have a router at home. It has, like, nine lights.

then.text: You saw the beacon glitch, right? Classic bad signal. I've seen it a hundred times. On YouTube.
then.speaker: Kevin

then.text: Why does everyone keep looking at me like that? I just got here. Again.
then.speaker: Kevin

else.text: Those gray hoodies are all over Dock 443. Probably a fashion thing. ...It's not a fashion thing, is it.
else.speaker: Kevin

then.text: PORT 443 - SECURE DOCK. Guarded by Pyrewall. The sign's lights stutter every few seconds.

else.text: PORT 443 - SECURE DOCK. Guarded by Pyrewall. All traffic must present a valid certificate.

port443_breach.text: Out over the water, the beacon over Port 443 stutters. Orange, white, orange...
For a second the dock gate hums like something big just walked through it. Nobody's there.
The beacon steadies. The harbor lights blink back on, one by one.
Third time this week. Harbor IT says it's just bad signal.
port443_breach.speaker: Dockworker

then.text: I was NOT standing right next to the gate when that happened. I was standing near it. Nearby. Adjacent.
then.speaker: Kevin

then.text: Anyway, it's obviously the router. I'd reboot the whole harbor, personally.
then.speaker: Kevin

port_help_desk_locked.text: The Help Desk doors are taped shut. A sign: "CLOSED FOR REWIRING. Somebody ran the new cables through the coffee machine."
A hand-written note below it: "Pop-up Help Desk in the shipping container next door. We're still open!"

popup_sign.text: POP-UP HELP DESK. Same great service. Smaller box.

popup_help_desk.speaker: Help Desk
popup_help_desk.text: Welcome to the Port City Help Desk! Well, the Port City Help Container.

popup_help_desk.speaker: Help Desk
popup_help_desk.choice: Want me to restore your Hexforged?

yes.speaker: Help Desk
yes.text: Have you tried turning it off and on again?

yes.speaker: Help Desk
yes.text: ...All fixed. Our real office is getting rewired, but our hands still work.

no.speaker: Help Desk
no.text: Ticket closed. Stay safe out there.

popup_supply.speaker: Supply Closet
popup_supply.text: Supply Closet, harbor branch! It's a shelf. In a container. Still counts.

then.text: Pyrewall's been guarding Port 443 since before I was born. Lately it flickers.
then.speaker: Dockworker

then.text: Harbor IT says it's bad signal. Bad signal doesn't usually come in through a locked gate.
then.speaker: Dockworker

else.text: See the orange beacon on Dock 443? That's Pyrewall. Nothing gets in without a valid certificate.
else.speaker: Dockworker

port_barista.speaker: Barista
port_barista.text: Port City runs on two things: cold brew and packet loss.

port_kid.speaker: Kid
port_kid.text: I caught a Calfiber in the tall cables by the water! It spouts light like a tiny lighthouse.

department_2_sign.text: NETWORKING DEPARTMENT. Certification trials inside. Please do not unplug anything.

basement_sign.text: EAST: THE BASEMENT. The valley's old server rooms and tape library. Authorized staff only.

department_2_welcome.text: Welcome to Networking! Ping's office is past the packet floor.
department_2_welcome.speaker: Receptionist

department_2_welcome.text: Step on a lane and it carries you like a packet until you land somewhere that isn't a lane.
department_2_welcome.speaker: Receptionist

department_2_welcome.text: Plan your hops. If you end up back down here, that's called a routing loop. We've all been there.
department_2_welcome.speaker: Receptionist

routing_notes.text: ROUTING NOTES: Every lane forwards you one way. The gaps between lanes are where you choose.
Shortest path isn't always the straight one. (Looking at you, Kevin. You've been looping since Tuesday.)

then.speaker: Ping
then.text: Latency's down, morale's up. Go on, {player}. Facilities will let you into the Basement now.

else.speaker: Ping
else.text: Every network's only as good as its weakest link. Let's find yours.

then.speaker: Facilities
then.text: Networking Cert? Ping vouched for you. Fine. Something's been chewing through the tape library down there.

then.speaker: Facilities
then.text: Bring a flashlight. And a Hard Reboot.

else.speaker: Facilities
else.text: The Basement's closed. Somebody's been messing with the old tape library.

else.speaker: Facilities
else.text: Get your Networking Cert from Ping first. Then we'll talk.
